title: Contraction of monoidal ideals in a log regular sharp chart
statement:
Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point, and let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Suppose that a chart $P\to M$ identifies $P$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$, and write $a:P\to(A,\cdot)$ for its structural map, with $P$ written additively. For every monoid ideal $J\subseteq P$ (a subset satisfying $J+P\subseteq J$, allowing the empty subset), let $JA=(a(j):j\in J)\subseteq A$. Then
$$a^{-1}(JA)=J.$$
Equivalently, a chart monomial $a(p)$ belongs to the ring ideal generated by the $a(j)$, $j\in J$, if and only if $p\in J$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 and its proof, printed p. 110: log ideals are recovered by contraction from their generated monoidal ideals; specialize at the geometric stalk in a chart identifying P with the sharp characteristic, so M_barx is P times A^units. The empty-ideal case also uses injectivity of alpha in the preceding conventions 3.4.1.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z[P]$ and let $K=a^{-1}(JA)$. Because $a$ is multiplicative and $JA$ is an ideal of $A$, $K$ is a monoid ideal: if $p\in K$ and $q\in P$, then $a(p+q)=a(p)a(q)\in JA$. Every $j\in J$ lies in $K$, so $J\subseteq K$. The current chart definition [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] identifies the chart monoid modulo the units of $A$ with the characteristic monoid; together with the sharp-chart lemma, this says that $P$ is finitely generated, integral and sharp and that every nonzero element of $P$ maps to a nonunit of the local ring $A$. Hence the ideal $\mathfrak m_P A$ generated by $P\setminus\{0\}$ is proper.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.1--3.4.3, printed pp. 110--111; reduce to a chart and use the injective structural map and sharp characteristic.

proof.text: For $I=J,K$, apply [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart] to get $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/IR,A)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] to $0\to IR\to R\to R/IR\to0$; its exactness makes $IR\otimes_RA\to R\otimes_RA=A$ injective, with multiplication image $IA$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to $JR\to KR\to KR/JR\to0$. Under the multiplication identifications its first map is the inclusion $JA\to KA$. By the definition $K=a^{-1}(JA)$, $KA\subseteq JA$, and $J\subseteq K$ gives the reverse inclusion. Hence this first map is surjective and $(KR/JR)\otimes_RA=0$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110, exact sequence (3.a) and the invocation of Kato (1994), 6.1(ii).

proof.text: If $J\subsetneq K$, apply [lem-trf-sharp-monoid-ideal-minimal-generators] to the finitely generated cancellative sharp monoid $P$ from step 1. It gives a finite monoid-ideal generating set for $K$ and an element $p\in K\setminus J$ outside $K+P^+$. Now [lem-trf-monomial-quotient-residue-surjection], applied to this $p$ and $f(e_q)=a(q)$, gives a surjection $(KR/JR)\otimes_RA\twoheadrightarrow A/\mathfrak m_PA$. The monoid ideal $J$ may be empty in both cited statements.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110; the sentence that $\mathbf Z[P]/\mathfrak m_P\mathbf Z[P]$ is a quotient of the monomial-ideal quotient.

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m_P A$ is proper by step 1, since every generator $a(q)$ for $q\ne0$ is a nonunit in the local ring $A$. Therefore $A/\mathfrak m_P A\ne0$, so the surjection in step 3 contradicts the vanishing obtained in step 2. Thus $K=J$, which is exactly $a^{-1}(JA)=J$. The argument includes $J=\varnothing$: then $JA=(0)$, and any nonempty $K$ would give the same nonzero quotient contradiction.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110; final contradiction and the empty-ideal case using 3.4.1.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 and proof, printed pp. 110--111; chart specialization at a geometric strict henselian stalk.

mathlib_searches.query: For a log regular scheme, a monoid ideal is recovered by contraction of the ideal it generates in the structure sheaf.
Extension and contraction give a bijection between logarithmic ideals and monoidal ring ideals on log regular schemes.
In a sharp chart of a logarithmically regular local ring, a monomial belongs to an extended monoid ideal exactly when its exponent belongs to that ideal.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-c583956cf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the re-split in full against the human re-split note of 2026-10-22, which asks for at least 2 comparable new nodes and a parent proof of at most 3000 characters with nothing shortened. The base proof in clones/live is identical to the report's 'Original step' texts. Steps 1 and 4 are kept verbatim. Step 2 is expanded, not shortened: it now cites the first-variable Tor long exact sequence to turn Kato's Tor_1 vanishing into IR⊗A≅IA, then uses tensor right exactness to get (KR/JR)⊗A=0. The 2011-character step 3 is spread over two statement-only unsplit nodes of comparable size. lem-trf-sharp-monoid-ideal-minimal-generators holds the Noetherian finite generation of the ideal and the choice of p∉J, p∉K+P^+, using the order from cancellation and sharpness. lem-trf-monomial-quotient-residue-surjection holds the monomial basis, ε as a ring map with kernel m (by sharpness), the well-definedness, R-linearity and surjectivity of φ_p, and the base change to A/mA. The parent proof is now a 2089-character assembly. Both new statements are true and self-contained: integrality is defined inline via the group completion of def-trf-fs-log-blowup, and the tensor product cites def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product. I tested them on P=0, P=N, and P=N² with J=(x), K=P (φ_0 is linear although x does not kill [1], so the earlier E3 annihilation error does not come back), on K=(x,y) with J=(x,y)², and on the monoid generated by 2 and 3. Neither node restates the parent. I searched the DAG with rg -L for monoid ideal, monomial ideal and Z[P]; the candidates lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ideal-coefficients-monomial, lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction, lem-per-log-regular-chart-monomial-tor and lem-per-monomial-module-tor-devissage are not duplicates. The Mathlib search records contain real outputs. Source: ILO VIII 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (PDF p. 116), whose sentence 'Z[P]/m_P Z[P] is a quotient of JZ[P]/IZ[P]' the new nodes spell out. lean.statement: theorem FineSaturatedLogScheme.monoidalIdeal_contraction (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (hregular : X.IsLogRegular) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) {P : Type u} [AddCommMonoid P] (W : X.scheme.Etale) (w : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).fiber.obj W) (c : Multiplicative P →* X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op W)) (hc : X.logStructure.IsChart W c) (hsharp : Function.Bijective (fun p : P ↦ (Associates.mk (X.logStructure.toEtalePrelogStructure.germ x W w (c (Multiplicative.ofAdd p))) : X.logStructure.characteristic x))) (J : Set P) (hJ : ∀ j ∈ J, ∀ p : P, j + p ∈ J) : (fun p : P ↦ X.logStructure.chartStrictHenselizationMap x W w c (Multiplicative.ofAdd p)) ⁻¹' (Ideal.span ((fun p : P ↦ X.logStructure.chartStrictHenselizationMap x W w c (Multiplicative.ofAdd p)) '' J) : Set (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing x)) = J
